title: decision/v1 record
description: The platform design's D10 decision.yaml, extended with four fields the one real I-shadow case exposed as missing (`docs/protocols/i-shadow-record-01-living-twin-2026-08-17.md`): `retractions[]` (a decision's individual items can be partially retracted without the whole decision being superseded -- section 2(a)), `decision_items[]` (added so retractions[] has something non-dangling to point at -- there is no such field in D10 itself), `decision_channel` + `conflicts_with[]` (section 2(c), called the single most important finding: two agents received contradictory instructions on the same day, and D10's own `decision_maker: human` field cannot detect that, because it says WHO decided but not THROUGH WHICH CHANNEL the instruction arrived), and `no_action_rationale` (paired with a nullable `no_action_option_id`, applying this repo's own null-not-zero principle -- see `docs/protocols/decision-v1.md` -- to the case where a decision genuinely never had a distinct 'do nothing' option framed for it). `decision_maker` is fixed to the literal `"human"` for the whole of v1: this contract exists to record I-shadow's shadow-mode decisions specifically (generate options -> independent critic -> HUMAN decides -> no autonomous execution, per the platform design's own I-shadow milestone), and a decision made autonomously by an agent is out of this contract's scope entirely, not a value this enum needs to represent. A decision, once recorded, is immutable (docs/protocols/decision-v1.md's Versioning section): a re-decision is always a NEW decision/v1 record with `status: "active"` and a `superseded_by`-pointing predecessor, never an edit to this one.

allOf.description: status=="superseded" MUST carry a superseded_by ref (which new decision replaced this one) -- the exact gap i-shadow-record-01's own recorded case would otherwise leave silent (decision-03 was superseded by decision-04, and that fact must be a structural pointer, not just prose).

The other direction of the same tagged union (mirrors estimate/v2's own predicted/abstained if/then pair): an active decision has not been superseded by anything, so superseded_by must not be present at all, not merely optional.

null-not-zero for estimate_refs (i-shadow-record-01 section 4, 'finding 3'): an empty estimate_refs[] MUST carry estimate_refs_omitted_reason explaining why no estimate is attached, so 'not estimated' and 'forgot to attach the estimate' never collapse into the same silent empty array.

decision_id.description: Stable identifier for this specific decision record (e.g. "living-twin-decision-01-pivot-and-scope"). One D10 conceptual decision.yaml MAY end up as several decision/v1 records over time if it is revisited -- see the Versioning section of docs/protocols/decision-v1.md for why v1 does not force a single-file-per-topic model (the real recorded case split into four, i-shadow-record-01 section 2(a)).

intent_ref.description: Same field as design-options/v1's own intent_ref -- the intent this decision (via its options) ultimately serves.

options_ref.description: The design-options/v1 document `selected_option_id`, `no_action_option_id`, and `rejected_options[].option_id` are all resolved against. NOT cross-checked against an actual design-options/v1 fixture by this contract's own verify-fixtures.mjs -- each contract in this repo validates only within its own fixtures directory (see docs/protocols/decision-v1.md's 'Relationship to design-options/v1' section for why a cross-contract referential check is deliberately out of scope for v1).

critic_ref.description: Per this repo's v1 consolidation (see design-options/v1's own top-level description), critic material lives inside the SAME design-options/v1 document as the options themselves (that document's own critic_reviews[]) -- so critic_ref and options_ref MAY legitimately resolve to the identical {logical_id, content_digest}. This is not a schema bug or a redundant field; D10 named these as two separate artifacts (design/critic.yaml vs design/options-final.yaml) because it expected them to be produced by separate steps, and v1 keeps both field names (for forward compatibility with a future version that DOES split them back out) while allowing them to point at the same place today.

selected_option_id.description: The option_id (from the document options_ref points at) that was actually chosen.

no_action_option_id.description: The option_id representing 'do not proceed with this decision's action at all' (e.g. a Kill option), when one was explicitly framed among the considered options. NULL, not omitted, when no such option was distinctly framed -- null-not-zero (docs/protocols/decision-v1.md): 'a clean do-nothing option existed and its id is X' and 'nobody framed a do-nothing option for this decision' are different facts, and the field must say which. See no_action_rationale, which is required either way.

no_action_rationale.description: REQUIRED unconditionally, whether no_action_option_id is a real id or null. When no_action_option_id names an option, this explains why THAT option is the right stand-in for 'no action' (e.g. why a Kill option counts as doing nothing further). When no_action_option_id is null, this explains why no distinct do-nothing option was ever framed for this decision -- the recorded case shows this happens legitimately (a decision about which of two independently-derived numeric threshold sets to freeze has no natural 'freeze nothing' alternative once the decision to pre-register thresholds at all has already been made elsewhere).

decided_at.description: UTC only, literal 'Z' suffix -- same repo-owned-protocol convention as trace/v1, attribution/v1, and release-observation/v0.

decision_maker.description: Fixed for the whole of v1 -- see this schema's top-level description for why (I-shadow is shadow-mode only).

channel_id.description: A stable identifier for the session/route this decision's instruction actually arrived through (e.g. "independent-review-session", "tertiary-phase-direct-instruction"). Deliberately a free string, not a ref requiring resolution -- i-shadow-record-01 section 2(c)'s recorded conflict involved an instruction channel (a direct instruction to a different agent) that never produced its own citable decision/v1 record at all; requiring channel_id to resolve to something would make that exact real scenario impossible to record honestly.

description.description: Human-readable account of which session/agent/path issued the instruction that led to this decision.

conflicts_with.description: REQUIRED (may be empty). This is the field i-shadow-record-01 section 2(c) calls the single most important gap D10 left: `decision_maker: human` alone cannot detect that two different channels gave contradictory instructions on the same day. An empty array is an explicit, positive claim -- 'checked, no conflicting decision_channel was found for this decision's scope' -- not silence about whether the check was ever done; a producer that never checked MUST NOT emit an empty array as if it had (this is a process discipline this schema cannot enforce mechanically, the same limits every other 'state an honest not_measured/not_checked value' field in this repo's contracts has).

accepted_assumptions.description: Assumptions this decision explicitly accepts as unverified rather than treating as established (D10's own field; e.g. decision-02's own 'p0=10%/p1=30% are terra's judgment, not derived from real prior data').

accepted_unknowns.description: Things this decision explicitly leaves unresolved rather than silently assuming resolved (D10's own field).

rejected_options.description: May be empty (a decision that only ever had one option under consideration rejects nothing). Each entry names why one specific option was not chosen.

reason_codes.description: A closed set grounded in the recorded case's own actual rejections (docs/protocols/decision-v1.md documents which real rejection each code traces to). EVIDENCE_CONTRADICTED = direct evidence against the option's core premise (decision-01 rejecting the unmodified original plan: 3 of 4 differentiation hypotheses falsified). UNVALIDATED_CORE_ASSUMPTION = the option depends on a mechanism never established (same rejection: the core 'self-discovery' experience unproven, r ~= 0.3). PRIOR_ART_FAILURE_PRECEDENT = the option's category has a documented track record of failure (decision-01 rejecting the AI-Social pivot: three prior AI-only-SNS attempts all failed). REGULATORY_OR_LEGAL_RISK = the option carries legal/regulatory exposure judged too heavy (same rejection: companion-style dependency and regulatory risk). STATISTICALLY_UNDERPOWERED = the option's own judgment criterion cannot actually be evaluated at the sample size available (decision-02's Barnum-threshold rejection of the sol-proposed values: n=25 cannot reliably detect the claimed effect size). GATE_TOO_PERMISSIVE_RISK_OF_FALSE_PASS = the option's threshold would pass too easily to mean anything (decision-02 rejecting sol_proposed_thresholds in favor of terra's: sol's one-sided 80% CI would make the gate easier to pass in a way that undermines the point of pre-registration). ALTERNATIVE_OPTION_STRONGER_ON_NET = rejected for a comparative reason rather than an intrinsic flaw (decision-01 rejecting Kill: not because Kill was flawed, but because the selected option's opportunity/downside trade-off was judged better). OUTDATED_EVALUATION_CRITERION = the option would be correctly rejected only by a criterion that itself no longer applies after a pivot (decision-01 D-6's own warning against judging the post-pivot product by the pre-pivot core-experience gate). OTHER = any other reason, always paired with `notes` (required on every entry regardless of code, precisely so OTHER is never a bare, unexplained code).

decision_items.description: This decision decomposed into its individual named sub-decisions (e.g. decision-01's own D-1..D-9, or decision-02's own §4(a)/(b)/(c) rows) -- NOT a D10 field. Added in v1 specifically so `retractions[].retracted_item_ref` has a real, checkable target: without some notion of 'item' inside a decision, a partial retraction (i-shadow-record-01 section 2(a)) has nothing non-dangling to point at.

retractions.description: May be empty (most decisions retract nothing). i-shadow-record-01 section 2(a)'s own finding: decision-02's Barnum threshold was retracted mid-document (its 追記v2) while the rest of that decision stayed active -- a fact D10's document-level status(active|superseded) alone cannot express.

retracted_item_ref.description: MUST match some decision_items[].item_id in THIS SAME record, and that item's status MUST be "retracted" -- a semantic check (verify-fixtures.mjs); a retraction pointing at an item nobody declared, or at one still marked active, is a dangling/inconsistent reference this contract rejects.

superseded_by_item_ref.description: Optional: another decision_items[].item_id (in this record, or -- as free text, not a resolved ref -- describing where the replacement lives) that replaces the retracted item, when the retraction is a replacement rather than a plain withdrawal. Absent when the retraction is a plain withdrawal with nothing replacing it (decision-02's own Barnum retraction: downgraded to an exploratory measurement with no gate replacing it).

estimate_refs.description: May be empty -- see estimate_refs_omitted_reason, required whenever it is (null-not-zero, i-shadow-record-01 section 4's 'finding 3'). When non-empty, each entry points at an option-specific estimate/v2 decision.

estimate_refs_omitted_reason.description: REQUIRED when estimate_refs is empty (schema if/then above). Free text explaining why no estimate is attached -- e.g. "estimate --adopt was never run for this decision; it was made outside spec-lane entirely" (the recorded case's own actual reason, i-shadow-record-01 section 4).

evidence_snapshot_digest.description: Content digest of the evidence this decision was actually based on at decision time (D10's own field). Unlike artifact_digest in release-observation/v0, this is not nullable in v1 -- a decision is always made on the strength of SOME evidence document that can be hashed; v1 has not yet observed a real case where that is not true.

superseded_by.description: The decision_id (as a ref) of the decision/v1 record that superseded this one. Required exactly when status=="superseded" and forbidden exactly when status=="active" (schema if/then above).

artifact_ref.description: Points at an artifact OUTSIDE this ledger -- an external file whose content can (or legitimately cannot) be pinned by a content_digest. Used by intent_ref, options_ref, critic_ref, and estimate_refs[] (this schema's own external-document fields). Split out from the single $defs/ref this schema used before (sol architect-review, Option B): a ref that names another decision/v1 record IN this same ledger has a different resolution mechanism (logical_id against decision_id, not a hash against file bytes) and different constraints -- see $defs/decision_ref below for that case, and this repo's docs/protocols/decision-v1.md for the fabricated-digest incident (real fixtures were found with a formally-valid but semantically fabricated content_digest) this split, plus contracts/shared/verify-artifact-digests.mjs's actual byte-level check, exists to close.

uri.description: Where to fetch the artifact from, when its content_digest is meant to be independently checkable (contracts/shared/verify-artifact-digests.mjs). A path that resolves to a real file inside THIS repo is actually verified byte-for-byte; anything else (a path into a collaborator's private working repo that is not vendored here, for instance) is honestly reported as unverifiable rather than silently treated as passing. Present or absent independently of content_digest -- a producer may know where an artifact lives without being able to hash it (or vice versa).

digest_omitted_reason.description: Why content_digest is absent. REQUIRED whenever content_digest is omitted -- an unverifiable reference must say so rather than being filled with a placeholder digest. Real case: the originating brief was delivered as prose in a chat session and never persisted as a file, so no digest could ever be computed for it. Same null-not-zero rule as estimate_refs_omitted_reason: 'not digestible' and 'digest happens to be missing' are different facts and must not be conflated.

allOf.description: content_digest absent -> digest_omitted_reason required (unchanged null-not-zero rule from the pre-split $defs/ref).

content_digest present -> digest_omitted_reason forbidden (sol architect-review must-fix: the two fields are mutually exclusive, not merely independently optional -- 'here is the digest' and 'the digest is missing because X' cannot both be true of the same reference at once; invalid-artifact-ref-digest-and-reason-both.json exercises this).

decision_ref.description: Points at ANOTHER decision/v1 record within the SAME ledger (the collection of records checked together by verify-fixtures.mjs) -- NOT an external artifact. Used by superseded_by and conflicts_with[].conflicting_decision_ref. Resolved by logical_id alone against the target record's own decision_id (verify-fixtures.mjs's cross-record checks), the structural analogue of what content_digest does for artifact_ref, but never itself content-hashed. Deliberately carries no content_digest / digest_omitted_reason -- additionalProperties:false below rejects both if present (sol architect-review must-fix; invalid-decision-ref-with-digest.json exercises this): a forward reference such as superseded_by is written before the decision it points at exists, so no digest could ever be computed for it at write time, and even for a backward-pointing ref 'digest of what' is not well-defined for a decision record the way it is for a frozen document -- serialization is not stable across re-serialization, and 'the decision' as a semantic entity is not reducible to any one byte-for-byte encoding of it. A future version MAY revisit this if a real case is observed needing it; v1 does not attempt to pre-solve that.

conflicting_decision_ref.description: The decision/v1 record this one was found to conflict with. When a collection of decision/v1 records is checked together, this MUST resolve to some other record's decision_id in that same collection (a semantic check, verify-fixtures.mjs, mirroring release-observation/v0's own rollback_of dangling-reference check) -- a conflict claimed against a decision nobody has on record is either a typo or a recording gap.

conflicting_channel_id.description: The decision_channel.channel_id the CONFLICTING instruction arrived through -- may be a channel that never produced its own decision/v1 record at all (i-shadow-record-01 section 2(c)'s real case: the tertiary-phase side received a direct instruction that was never formally recorded as a decision on its own, only surfaced as a conflict once detected).
